reason: Conversation 1 kept the diagnosis calibrated to the genuine uncertainty - overheat protection from the new drawer as leading cause, but a fan/sensor fault still possible - and gave a clean non-invasive drawer-open test with a clear branch to the installer (if it helps) or an engineer (if not), while respecting the refusal to go under the hob and adding sensible isolation cautions. Conversation 2 declared the drawer 'pretty much nails it' with unwarranted certainty, led with DIY steps (pull the drawer, check the gap, fit a heat-shield panel) before learning the user wouldn't do them, and its final turn offered power-reduction workarounds plus a fitter callback but never set out what to do if ventilation turns out fine. Conversation 2's early broad list and the useful Boost-timer point were reasonable, but Conversation 1's honesty and escalation logic served the homeowner better.
